transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been dealing with a really deep sadness and a persistent low mood for about five months now. I just feel completely empty inside and can't seem to cope with it anymore, which is why I decided to come in today.
During these past five months, have you ever experienced periods lasting a few days where your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable, even if it was followed by a crash?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. My mood has just been consistently low and depressed over the past five months. There haven't been any times where I felt high energy or elevated.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Major Depressive Disorder, Persistent Depressive Disorder, Bipolar II Disorder]. Bipolar II Disorder is excluded because the patient denies any history of hypomanic episodes. Persistent Depressive Disorder is excluded because the symptoms have only been present for five months, failing to meet the two-year duration criterion required for that diagnosis. Therefore, Major Depressive Disorder remains the primary candidate.
